headline: KOREA BANS **AI**
FAKE DOCTOR ADS
cover.hook_pick_reason: No reader-impact hook: AI Times states the ban and its penalties but no effect on what ordinary viewers will see, pay or risk, and a Korea-only ad rule cannot be promised to change viewers' feeds. The headline states the news itself (Korea bans ads with AI-made fake doctors, from Nov 27) and every word is supported by slides 1 and 2. The number options are vivid but narrower: 46 is a subset of 420 improper ads, and 8.1bn won is one company's sales in one case. The 'suspended' option covers only the penalty, not the ban.

slides.title: Korea bans AI 'experts' in ads
body: From **Nov 27**, ads in which AI-made virtual doctors or professors recommend food, drugs or cosmetics are banned in South Korea. The rule for medical devices follows on **Dec 10**.

slides.title: The regulator rewrote its rules
body: South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, the regulator for food, drugs and cosmetics, said on Nov 26 it revised its enforcement rules. Banned: ads that mislead consumers into thinking a **fake AI expert** endorses a product.

slides.title: Violators can be shut for months
body: For food, a first violation means a **15-day business suspension**, a second 1 month, a third 2 months. Cosmetics are tougher: from 2 months for a first violation to **12 months** for a fourth or later.

slides.title: 420 improper ads in 9 months
body: The Korea Consumer Agency, a government consumer-protection body, monitored YouTube ads from October last year to June this year. It found **420 improper ads**, including **46** that used AI to impersonate doctors, pharmacists or nurses.

slides.title: One AI doctor sold 8.1bn won
body: In June, a company that sold **8.1 billion won** of products was referred to prosecutors. It used an AI fake doctor to claim 'body age reduction' and anti-aging effects.

slides.title: Critics say penalties are light
body: Some critics say the penalties are not heavy compared with the **sales made on platforms** in a short time. Whether the ban reaches the platforms themselves is not stated in the report.

facts.text: Ads in which AI-made virtual doctors or professors recommend food, drugs or cosmetics are banned from the 27th.
The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety said on the 26th it revised enforcement rules so that ads that mislead consumers into thinking fake AI experts endorse a product are banned.
The food, pharmaceutical and cosmetics laws take effect on the 27th; the medical devices law takes effect on December 10.
Food: a first violation means a 15-day business suspension, a second 1 month, a third 2 months.
Cosmetics carry the heaviest penalties, from 2 months for a first violation to 12 months for a fourth or later.
The Korea Consumer Agency monitored YouTube ads for 9 months (October last year to June this year) and found 420 improper ads, including 46 that used AI to impersonate doctors, pharmacists or nurses.
In June, a company that sold 8.1 billion won worth of products using an AI fake doctor to claim 'body age reduction' and anti-aging effects was referred to prosecutors.
Some critics say the penalties are not heavy compared with the sales made on platforms in a short time.

caption:
South Korea will ban ads where AI-made fake doctors and professors recommend food, drugs or cosmetics from Nov 27.

The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety revised its enforcement rules, AI Times reports. Violators can face business suspension, and the Korea Consumer Agency found 46 YouTube ads using AI to impersonate medical staff.

→ Ban starts Nov 27 for food, drugs and cosmetics; Dec 10 for medical devices
→ Food: 15-day suspension for a first violation; cosmetics: 2 to 12 months
→ 420 improper YouTube ads found in 9 months, 46 with AI-faked doctors, pharmacists or nurses
